ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the sinusoidal AC circuit shown in the figure, an inductance with reactance of \(10\,\Omega\) and a load \(Z\) are connected in series. If the voltmeters \((V1)\), \((V2)\), and \((V)\) all show the same value, then the load \(Z =\) ______ \(\angle -30^{\circ}\,\Omega\).
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a sinusoidal AC series circuit, with voltage u marked on the left, and a total voltmeter V connected between the upper and lower ends. In the main branch on the right, the upper part is an inductive reactance labeled 10 Ω, and the lower part is a load Z connected in series. Voltmeter V1 is connected across the two ends of the 10 Ω inductor, and voltmeter V2 is connected across the two ends of the load Z. Then reason: Let the series current be I. The magnitude of the inductor voltage is |V1| = |I·j10| = 10|I|; the magnitude of the load voltage is |V2| = |I·Z| = |I||Z|; the magnitude of the total voltage is |V| = |I·(Z + j10)|. The problem states that the readings of the three voltmeters are the same, therefore 10|I| = |I||Z| = |I||Z + j10|. Eliminating |I| gives |Z| = 10 Ω. The problem gives the form as Z = ____ ∠ -30° Ω, so the blank is the impedance magnitude 10. Check: If Z = 10∠-30° Ω, then Z = 8.66 - j5, Z + j10 = 8.66 + j5, and its magnitude is also 10 Ω, satisfying that the readings of the three voltmeters are equal.
